projects.title: Demand forecasting tool
projects.blurb: Replaced a hand-built monthly spreadsheet with a model the planning team actually trusts.
projects.content:
## The problem

Every month, three people spent the better part of a week rebuilding the same forecast by hand. The numbers were never reproducible, and nobody could explain a variance after the fact.

## What I did

- Interviewed the planners to understand which adjustments they were making by instinct, and why
- Built a baseline model, then added the two seasonal effects that actually mattered
- Shipped a review step so planners could override a number and have that override recorded

## Result

Forecast prep dropped from five days to under an hour. More importantly, every number now has a traceable reason behind it.

## What I would change

I over-invested in model accuracy early on. The thing that made adoption work was the override log, and I built that last.

projects.title: Customer insights dashboard
projects.blurb: One shared view of customer behaviour, replacing four teams' conflicting reports.
projects.content:
## The problem

Four teams each maintained their own definition of an active customer. Meetings started with an argument about whose number was right.

## What I did

- Ran a short workshop to agree on one definition, in writing
- Modelled the metric once in dbt so every report reads from the same source
- Built a single dashboard and deprecated the other reports deliberately, with notice

## Result

The definitional argument stopped. Adoption was helped more by turning the old reports off than by building the new one.

projects.title: Supply chain optimisation
projects.blurb: A routing and inventory model that found meaningful annual savings.
projects.content:
## The problem

Stock was allocated to warehouses using a rule written years earlier that nobody had revisited.

## What I did

- Framed allocation as a linear programme with real capacity and lead-time constraints
- Validated against a year of historical data before proposing any change
- Presented the result as a range, not a single number, so operations could weigh the risk

## Result

The recommended reallocation was adopted for two regions and produced measurable savings in the first two quarters.
